subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum + spillover policy options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet.singh@acme.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum + spillover policy options

Hi Jaspreet,

Hope you're doing well — as we approach your Apr 1 renewal, I wanted to propose a concise addendum that covers the Dedicated capacity expansion we discussed on the last call. TL;DR: Acme requested 4 additional reserved GPUs and clarity on burst/spillover behavior during traffic spikes.

Attached is a draft addendum (Redwood_Dedicated_Addendum_v3.pdf) and a short capacity appendix that maps expected concurrent workloads to suggested pool size (Capacity_Appendix_ACME.xlsx). High-level options for burst behavior:

- Option A (Preferred): Reserved + soft spillover. Add 4 reserved GPUs to your Dedicated pool. Allow on-demand spillover to hosted capacity when utilization exceeds reserved capacity, subject to a configurable daily budget cap. We’ll set an automatic hard cap fallback if the budget is exhausted to avoid runaway spend.
- Option B: Hard cap only. Add 4 reserved GPUs; no spillover. Traffic above the hard cap will get throttled/failover to reduced throughput mode.
- Option C: Dedicated-only burst buffer. Keep everything in Dedicated by provisioning a larger reserved buffer (higher monthly commit) with no on-demand usage.

Key things for Acme to confirm: your preferred burst approach (A/B/C), the daily spend cap you’re comfortable with for spillover, and whether you want a throughput guarantee for the reserved baseline.

Proposal ask / next steps:
1) Confirm a preferred option by next Tue (Feb 24) so we can finalize pricing.
2) If Option A — give us a daily budget cap number and the account users who can approve exceeded spend.
3) If you want a reserved throughput SLA we’ll lock baseline throughput and include it in the addendum.

I’ve looped in Rishi (sales lead) and Marissa (customer success) for pricing and go-live coordination. Happy to hop on a quick call if it’s easier.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Capacity_Appendix_ACME.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet.singh@acme.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.io
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 10:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum + spillover policy options

Naomi — thanks for the summary and the draft. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and infra: 

1) For Option A (soft spillover) can you confirm how billing is metered for on-demand resources — is it per token, per GPU-hour, or a blended view? We need a unit we can map back to our daily budget control systems.

2) If we pick spillover, who enforces the hard cap? Can we configure automated cutoffs with email alerts to our procurement alias?

3) Throughput guarantee request: we need a baseline that supports our nightly batch generation (roughly 3M tokens over a 2 hour window). Can you map the baseline GPUs to a throughput figure we can vet with our infra team?

4) SOC 2 / evidence: procurement still requests updated SOC 2 and audit window info for the Dedicated control plane. Please send the latest report or pointer.

We’d prefer Option A if we can get a clear billing unit and an automated hard cap that prevents surprises. For the daily spillover budget — preliminary ask is $6,000/day but we need to confirm with finance.

Thanks — Jaspreet
Jaspreet Singh
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp.
jaspreet.singh@acme.io
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum + spillover policy options

Naomi / team — quick internal thread with recommendations before we reply to Acme.

Notes from infra/solutions (Dev):
- Billing: spillover is best expressed as per-GPU-hour equivalent (hosted vCPU/GPU runtime) so Acme can map to cloud budget lines. We compute on-demand spillover cost as a blended token/GPU-hour; for commercial proposals we show a $/GPU-hour and an approximate $/M tokens for comparison.
- Hard cap enforcement: we support a configurable daily budget cap at account level (automated cutoff + email notifications to configured aliases). We can set a soft throttle at 80% and then cut to hard cap once the budget is reached.
- Throughput mapping: baseline reserved pool (their current + 4 GPUs) maps to an estimated sustained throughput of ~30,000 tokens/sec aggregated for typical generation prompt sizes (this is conservative; we will validate with their nightly job profile). For the 3M tokens over 2 hours request, that’s ~416 tokens/sec sustained — well inside the baseline.

Commercial proposal (Marissa / Rishi):
- Addendum pricing: incremental monthly commit for 4x A100-equivalent GPUs = $XX,XXX/month (I’ll insert final $ before send).
- If Option A, spillover bill rate = $/GPU-hour with a 20% premium to hosted public rates; we’ll show an example: $12.50/GPU-hour equivalent with a notional token conversion. Daily spend cap enforced at account level.
- SLA: baseline reserved throughput SLA 99.9% uptime for reserved pool with credits tied to missed baseline throughput targets; burst availability is best-effort and not SLA-backed.

Recommendation: reply to Acme proposing Option A with the automated budget cap (we can set to $6k/day as requested) and include the SOC 2 pointer. Also propose a brief validation window post-renewal: 14 days of telemetry where we tune batch/kv-cache settings to meet their throughput.

I’ll pull final numbers for the incremental commit and draft the small addendum language to lock the guarantees.

-Rishi
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jaspreet Singh <jaspreet.singh@acme.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.io
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 14:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum + spillover policy options

Jaspreet — thanks for the rapid feedback and the initial budget guidance. Per our internal review here’s the concrete proposal for your approval: 

Summary (what we’ll include in the addendum):
- Reserved expansion: +4 A100-equivalent GPUs to your existing Dedicated pool, starting at renewal (Apr 1).
- Billing for spillover: on-demand spillover metered as $/GPU-hour equivalent. We will include an illustrative token conversion in the addendum for finance mapping. Example rate (illustrative): $12.50/GPU-hour equivalent.
- Budget cap / enforcement: account-level daily spend cap configurable in the Console. Default enforcement flow we propose: soft throttle at 80% of the cap (email notify to procurement@acme.io + account admins), and an automatic hard cutoff when the cap is reached. We will set the cap to $6,000/day per your note unless you instruct otherwise.
- Throughput: baseline reserved pool will carry a reserved throughput commitment sufficient to support your nightly 3M-token job; our estimate maps their baseline (current pool + 4 GPUs) to ~30,000 tokens/sec aggregated. Baseline SLA: 99.9% availability for reserved pool throughput. Burst capacity is best-effort and not SLA-backed.
- Validation window: 14 days of post-renewal telemetry tuning included; Redwood will action batch and cache adjustments during that window.
- Compliance: SOC 2 pointer: https://redwood.com/compliance/soc2-2025-report (we’ll send the artifact under NDA if procurement needs it).

Next steps / ask from Acme:
1) Confirm Option A (soft spillover) and the $6,000/day cap or propose an alternate cap.
2) Confirm the list of approvers for budget overrides (who should get the alert emails).
3) Sign the addendum (DocuSign link below) once you’ve confirmed; we’ll then lock pricing and schedule the Apr 1 change.

DocuSign (draft addendum): https://www.docusign.com/prepare/12345-addendum
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/2000/deal/ACME-2026-RNW-42

If that all looks good I’ll attach the redlined addendum and route to DocuSign. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if your team wants to review any of the enforcement flows live.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
